transcript.text: Maestro Salieri, if you please, take a seat. I must be candid with you. Your symptoms — the trembling, the headaches, the confusion you've described — do not, I regret to say, fit a single clear diagnosis. It could well be a severe case of nervous exhaustion, brought on by your immense dedication to your duties and the relentless pace of the Court. Or, I must also consider, it could be the early signs of something more serious affecting the brain. For now, I must insist you reduce your conducting duties significantly, and you must submit to further examination over the coming weeks. At this juncture, I cannot yet say whether your hands will recover their former steadiness.
